dataset.description: Catalogue of vertebrate and plant collections in the Laboratory of Mineralogy and Paleontology of the University of Latvia contains data on the Late Devonian, Late Famennian fossil vertebrates and plants from the Ketleri Formation.

distribution.title: The main purpose of the data collection is to gather information on the vertebrate and plant fossils from the Upper Devonian, Upper Famennian deposits of Latvia, to ensure possibilities to compare with materials from elsewhere, e.g., Greenland, South Africa and Pennsylvania. Catalogues of the collections of the Laboratory of Mineralogy and Paleontology of UL originate from the material gathered by the project team.

dataset.title: Catalogue of collection of the Late Famennian vertebrates from Latvia in the MinPal laboratory

dataset.description: This data set contains photogrammetric images, laser-and-optical-scanned and CT-scanned images of the Late Devonian fossil vertebrates and plants from Latvia. The purpose of this description is to demonstrate kinds of data stored within the collection.

distribution.title: The main purpose of the data collection is to gather information on the vertebrate and plant fossils from the Devonian deposits of Latvia, to ensure possibilities to compare with materials from elsewhere, e.g., Greenland, South Africa and Pennsylvania. Images of vertebrate and plant fossils like photogrammetric models, models from the laser or optical scans and computer tomographic models are produced by various equipment by the members of the project team, as well as by our collaborators in Sweden and Great Britain.

dataset.title: Image collection of the Late Famennian fossils from Latvia

dmp.description: The origin and early evolution of tetrapods from fish ancestors is one of the most important questions in vertebrate evolution. The main aim of the project is to elucidate diversification trends of Late Devonian tetrapods by comparing the composition and palaeoecological features of fossil vertebrate assemblages from the Late Devonian, Late Famennian deposits of Latvia, Greenland and South Africa.
